generic: Oak pays for two loaves every Friday. He's been alone in that lab for twenty years.
The foghorn went at noon. My Growlithe was under the table a full minute before I heard it.
I leave the latch low for my Growlithe. He can let himself in. Took him two summers to learn it.
rivalAhead: Your friend asked which one you picked. I told them to go ask you. That's a bit of a sore point, is it?
They've been standing by the gate long enough to wear a hole in it. Shall I tell them you’re coming?

generic: See the Machop with the red bandanna? He hasn't missed a shift in twelve years. The foreman can't say that.
They packed the old mine entrance with concrete. There's a hook there for the night men's coats. Nobody's taken it down.
You can write your name in the dust on my steps if you're quick. Rain's coming.
preGym: I've got lunch for the Gym staff. A bag for each round. You brought enough for your party?
Go to the Dojo if you've got time. They'll let you ask a daft question without making you ask it in front of everybody.
postGym: They stuck your result over the overtime sheet. Don't pull it down. We can finally pretend we didn't see it.
Is that your first? Keep the pin closed when it’s in your pocket. I still have the scar.

generic: The stone seller buys a bag of sweets for the Geodude that hauls her stock. He picks the green ones out.
There's an empty Egg basket by the inn stove. When the staff mop, they lift it with both hands.
The Tutor once spent a whole lunch break teaching a Magikarp to go back in its Ball without sulking.
preGym: Through the café courtyard for the Gym. Go round the old Growlithe under table three. He's got one good eye and you’re on the wrong side of it.
The Move Tutor's kettle just went. If you want one last lesson, now's a good time.
postGym: Did the crowd seem a bit thin to you? I heard them from the cafe. The announcer still thanked a full house.
Your partner's still looking back at the Gym. Mine used to do that. I think she liked the applause.

generic: There's a survey notebook in the academy's lost-property drawer. I put my name down to borrow it. My signature was already there.
The students practice in the small lecture room. Help them shift the desks and they'll give you the first match.
There's a bell for the last class and one for the gate. When they go together, the whole town gets its coat on.
preGym: The students have a picture of every challenger on the practice board. Good luck finding them admitting whose idea that was.
If the lecture's still on, take the side door. The Gym's across the yard.
postGym: A lad came into the café with your last turn drawn on a napkin. He wanted me to put it on the till where his mum would see.
There's a bit of chalk on your sleeve. Leave it there until you get out of town. We could use the luck.
rivalAhead: Your rival borrowed a practice room. I waited to lock up. Through the wall I heard them apologize to their partner.
They asked which road you were taking. I asked which road they were taking. Seemed only fair.

generic: Don't use the service lift unless you work here. There's a floor marked RETURNS and the button lights up on its own.
The Department Store clerk knows every floor. Ask them. The arrows take you past the perfume even if you're buying potions.
I caught a Meowth sleeping in a sale basket. Manager put him on a shelf with a sign that says DISPLAY ONLY. He's got regulars.
preGym: The Gym entrance is at street level. Anybody offering you a lift upstairs wants to sell you something.
Get your supplies before the crowd pours out. I put my hip out in the Department Store after last week's match.
postGym: You were on all the televisions. Different timing on each one. I got to see the winning move three times without turning my head.
Somebody wrote your score on a shop window. I told the cleaner to leave it up until closing.

generic: Follow the boards to the ranger huts for the Safari Zone. Follow the carpet for the Game Corner. Don't swap halfway in wet boots.
Ranger counted nine Krabby onto the bank this morning. Counted eight back. The ninth was under his hat.
My brother puts the train fare in his left pocket before he goes to the Game Corner. Now he wears a coat without a left pocket.
preGym: The wind puts the boardwalk out after sundown. If you're headed to the Gym, go along the shopfronts.
Saw them chalking the court this morning. Looked like half the town had gone down there just to watch the lines go on.
postGym: The ranger from the far gate came out when he heard the crowd. He asked who won. I think he wanted an excuse to take his hat off.
Get out by the lake path if the Game Corner crowd's still crossing. You can hear your own partner out there.

generic: Pick a bay number if you're meeting someone after work. There are eleven signs that say EXIT and only ten gates.
Old Champion's on the screen again. I wish they'd fix it. My dad's standing behind him and he keeps looking down to check the time.
We leave dry blankets on the freight fence. In winter, the Trubbish bring back the ones nobody took.
preGym: The arena doors open early. Ask for the warm-up room if your partner doesn't like the speakers.
My shift put together enough for one ticket. They picked my name out of a lunch bag. If you hear a fool shouting, that's me.
postGym: There you are. You're shorter than you look on the square screen. I hope you don't mind hearing that from everybody today.
There was a man in the next row who wouldn't stand for anybody. He stood up for your partner.
rivalAhead: Your rival asked when the gate shuts. I told them the last freight's at eleven. They didn't ask about trains.
The Gym clerk said there was a note for you. They're keeping it under the blotter so it won't walk off.

generic: Colress keeps saying the roof lab can hear Electric types through the interference. At least shut the door if you go and listen.
There are two lamps by the relay hut. The keeper took one away last winter. We still see two from here.
If the rail turns white, take the lower path. Your boots will tell you why before I can.
preGym: Go while Buck's at his bench if you want your partner's stats looked over. He leaves when his tea goes cold.
Only top step's iced over. Put the hand with the badge case in your pocket and hold the rail with the other.
postGym: Come have a seat with the old lot. You can tell them how it went. They promise to let you finish before they tell you how theirs went.
That's the cathedral bell, over the ridge. Don't count the rings if you're waiting for the wind to stop.

generic: There are four patches in the altar cloth. My mum put in the little red one. Bells went off while she was threading the needle.
Ask the keeper about the gate if you're leaving tonight. He'll make you take a lamp. Don't argue. He gave me one once.
The little bell has a cracked lip. You can tell it's ours all the way from Victory Road.
preGym: I keep the kettle on when there's a challenger inside. Go on. I'll have a cup for you when you come out.
The keeper can hear you at the door. If you knock twice, he's liable to think you're staff.
postGym: Eight? Here. Wrap that case in a sock. The clasp'll start rattling three miles out.
A masked traveler asked whether you were still here. I said I'd have to see your face first if I was going to tell you a thing.

generic: Check in at the second door. First one's the broadcast booth. They won't turn off that red light once you’re in there.
My brother was a long time in his first chamber. I walked around this building till the soles went soft. Got a seat this year.
The clerk polishes the empty frame at the end every morning. Keeps a little rag on the ledge just for it.
The Hall got your name right. I looked. There’s still somebody waiting for you down the corridor.
Didn't they turn off the hall microphones? I could hear somebody checking the levels as I came out.
I've still got your coat behind the desk. You can go down that corridor and I'll keep it here till you're through.
There's usually a spare seat in the Crucible. The one by the service door costs you a coat.
Bring your badge case if you want. The Frontier clerk makes the Champion sign the same card they make everybody sign.
The night clerk puts a saucer out by the back door. Nobody's seen what drinks out of it. They know when it's empty.
